channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Apple Store Creator on New Book and Retail’s AI Future
item.description: Ron Johnson, Creator of the Apple Store and author of the new book "Shop Different: How Retail Revealed Apple's Genius" takes a look at the strategy behind the iconic Apple Store and how Apple has transformed over more than 50 years. He begins by reflecting on the long-running debate over whether the internet would kill retail, suggesting that concern was overstated. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Live Nation Has Received $420 Million in Subsidies From US Cities: Study
item.description: A new report digs into the subsidies that local governments provide the entertainment giant
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: MSCI CEO: Investors Are Putting Money Everywhere
item.description: Henry Fernandez, Chairman and CEO at MSCI, discusses Oracle’s force majeure notice in the context of heavy borrowing and large investments tied to the long-term AI story. He goes on to talk about global inflation that may linger and the Fed may need to hike again, framing the segment around pressure in markets and the cost of capital. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Goldman Sachs Is Underweight Hyperscalers on Debt Supply Surge
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s Lindsay Rosner says the bank’s asset management arm is underweight on the biggest artificial intelligence borrowers as a flood of issuance washes over the market.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Tayeb

item.title: Maria Vassalou on Rising Government Debt, Trump-XI Summit
item.description: Maria Vassalou, Head of the Pictet Research Institute, discusses the deepening global bond rout and Treasury market pressure. She goes on to talk about the growing talk of a U.S. debt reckoning is being overstated too soon, setting up a broader conversation about whether current market concerns are getting ahead of the underlying economic reality. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Principal CIO on Inflation Concerns, Rising Bond Yields
item.description: George Maris of Principal Asset Management discusses the growing pressure on equities from the bond market. The conversation focuses on whether the recent rise in yields, both overall and in terms of the speed of the move over the past few months, has reached a level where stock investors should be increasingly concerned. He speaks to Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Biology Lab Enzyme Discovery Draws Caution From Scientists
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s announcement that its Claude AI model discovered an enzyme system that resembled an earlier breakthrough gene editing technology was met with caution by some experts in the field, who suggested the company oversold its significance.
item.dc:creator: Robert Langreth

item.title: Odd Lots: Maybe AI Won’t Kill Us All — Just Some of Us
item.description:
Big Tech has been sounding alarms about the risk of AI causing human extinction but there are also skeptics who dismiss the notion, like former US Federal Trade Commissioner Alvaro Bedoya, who referenced the Black Death to dismiss warnings of existential risks.
On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast recorded live at the Vermont Hollywood theater, Rachel Karten, author of the Link in Bio newsletter, and Taylor Lorenz, founder of User Mag, talk about the possibility of AI killing all humans, or maybe just some. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Strikes $12 Billion AI Computing Deal With Akamai
item.description: Anthropic PBC has signed an $11.6 billion, seven-year contract with Akamai Technologies Inc. for computing power, adding to the AI developer’s growing list of data center deals.
item.dc:creator: Lynn Doan

item.title: AI-Tied Debt Seeing Higher Costs
item.description: Lindsay Rosner, Head of Multi Sector Fixed Income investing at Goldman Sachs and Milwood Hobbs, Deputy CIO Strategic Credit Platform at Oaktree Capital speak with Scarlet Fu "Bloomberg Real Yield." They discuss growing AI-related debt and tightening high-yield spreads. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft’s Suleyman Says Industry Needs ‘Red Line’ for AI
item.description: The software giant’s AI chief also thinks the government should help “drive” the process of evaluating models.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: AI Policy An Opportunity For 'Bipartisan Step Forward,' Says Miriam Vogel
item.description: Miriam Vogel, president and CEO of EqualAI, said that she heard very little partisan rhetoric when she testified on the impact of AI in front of lawmakers and described the creation of AI policy as an 'opportunity for a bipartisan step forward.' Vogel also weighed in on the AI race between the US and China, saying that China is using a 'whole of government approach' with the technology. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Takes Center Stage From Oracle to the White House
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Oracle's latest move to protect itself from mounting costs on a massive New Mexico data center facing regulatory setbacks and local opposition. Plus, Meta comes out with a new palm-sized device for using its popular new AI assistant, Muse; and all eyes are on President Trump and China's President Xi Jinping as they meet in the White House and discuss AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Darktrace CEO: AI Agents Are the New ‘Insider Threat’
item.description: Darktrace CEO Ed Jennings says AI agents are becoming a new kind of “insider threat” as companies rapidly deploy autonomous systems with access to sensitive data and infrastructure. As Darktrace launches new tools to track shadow AI, agent identities and behavior, Jennings discusses why cybersecurity is racing to catch up with adoption, what happens when agents act beyond their intended roles, and why behavioral monitoring could help companies safely capture the benefits of AI. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Emerges as a Flashpoint in Trump-Xi Talks
item.description: The US-China AI race is emerging as a key issue surrounding talks between President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, as Chinese open-weight models close the gap with leading US systems. Rhodium Group’s Reva Goujon discusses tensions over AI safety and export controls, divisions within the Trump administration over potential guardrails, and how technology restrictions, critical minerals and Taiwan factor into the broader US-China negotiations. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Bets on AI, Devices for Its Next Chapter
item.description: Meta is experimenting with new ways to move beyond its social media roots, from the fast-growing Muse AI assistant to smart glasses and its new palm-sized Charm device. eMarketer Senior Analyst Minda Smiley discusses whether Muse marks a turning point for Meta’s AI strategy, why the company is testing multiple hardware form factors, and whether its latest products have staying power or risk becoming another short-lived technology fad. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dutch Prime Minister Has Discussed MATCH Act With Trump
item.description: Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten had discussions on legislation which would further restrict ASML Holding NV’s sales in China with President Donald Trump. Jetten told Bloomberg Television, “I’m pretty sure we come to some agreement that is workable for each and every one.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Attorney General Probes Data Center Projects Over Water Usage
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton is investigating hundreds of data center developments over whether they’re complying with water-use reporting requirements.
item.dc:creator: Julia Amann and Joe Lovinger

item.title: HouseCanary Files Bankruptcy to Collect $260 Million From Rocket
item.description: Property data provider HouseCanary Inc. filed for bankruptcy to buy time to collect more than $260 million from affiliates of Rocket Mortgage, which were accused of stealing a computer model used to quickly value homes for real estate investors and mortgage brokers.
item.dc:creator: Steven Church

item.title: Qualcomm Renews Licensing Pact With Apple Starting in 2027
item.description: Qualcomm Inc., the largest producer of smartphone processors, renewed its global licensing pact with Apple Inc. starting April 1, signaling that the iPhone maker will remain a customer for now.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Frier and Nick Turner
